@dev Contract module that helps prevent reentrant calls to a function.
 Inheriting from `ReentrancyGuard` will make the {nonReentrant} modifier
 available, which can be applied to functions to make sure there are no nested
 (reentrant) calls to them.
 Note that because there is a single `nonReentrant` guard, functions marked as
 `nonReentrant` may not call one another. This can be worked around by making
 those functions `private`, and then adding `external` `nonReentrant` entry
 points to them.
 TIP: If you would like to learn more about reentrancy and alternative ways
 to protect against it, check out our blog post
 https://blog.openzeppelin.com/reentrancy-after-istanbul/[Reentrancy After Istanbul].

@dev Prevents a contract from calling itself, directly or indirectly.
 Calling a `nonReentrant` function from another `nonReentrant`
 function is not supported. It is possible to prevent this from happening
 by making the `nonReentrant` function external, and making it call a
 `private` function that does the actual work.

@dev Returns true if `account` is a contract.
 [IMPORTANT]
 ====
 It is unsafe to assume that an address for which this function returns
 false is an externally-owned account (EOA) and not a contract.
 Among others, `isContract` will return false for the following
 types of addresses:
  - an externally-owned account
  - a contract in construction
  - an address where a contract will be created
  - an address where a contract lived, but was destroyed
 ====
 [IMPORTANT]
 ====
 You shouldn't rely on `isContract` to protect against flash loan attacks!
 Preventing calls from contracts is highly discouraged. It breaks composability, breaks support for smart wallets
 like Gnosis Safe, and does not provide security since it can be circumvented by calling from a contract
 constructor.
 ====

@dev Replacement for Solidity's `transfer`: sends `amount` wei to
 `recipient`, forwarding all available gas and reverting on errors.
 https://eips.ethereum.org/EIPS/eip-1884[EIP1884] increases the gas cost
 of certain opcodes, possibly making contracts go over the 2300 gas limit
 imposed by `transfer`, making them unable to receive funds via
 `transfer`. {sendValue} removes this limitation.
 https://diligence.consensys.net/posts/2019/09/stop-using-soliditys-transfer-now/[Learn more].
 IMPORTANT: because control is transferred to `recipient`, care must be
 taken to not create reentrancy vulnerabilities. Consider using
 {ReentrancyGuard} or the
 https://solidity.readthedocs.io/en/v0.5.11/security-considerations.html#use-the-checks-effects-interactions-pattern[checks-effects-interactions pattern].

@dev Performs a Solidity function call using a low level `call`. A
 plain `call` is an unsafe replacement for a function call: use this
 function instead.
 If `target` reverts with a revert reason, it is bubbled up by this
 function (like regular Solidity function calls).
 Returns the raw returned data. To convert to the expected return value,
 use https://solidity.readthedocs.io/en/latest/units-and-global-variables.html?highlight=abi.decode#abi-encoding-and-decoding-functions[`abi.decode`].
 Requirements:
 - `target` must be a contract.
 - calling `target` with `data` must not revert.
 _Available since v3.1._

@dev Returns the address that signed a hashed message (`hash`) with
 `signature` or error string. This address can then be used for verification purposes.
 The `ecrecover` EVM opcode allows for malleable (non-unique) signatures:
 this function rejects them by requiring the `s` value to be in the lower
 half order, and the `v` value to be either 27 or 28.
 IMPORTANT: `hash` _must_ be the result of a hash operation for the
 verification to be secure: it is possible to craft signatures that
 recover to arbitrary addresses for non-hashed data. A safe way to ensure
 this is by receiving a hash of the original message (which may otherwise
 be too long), and then calling {toEthSignedMessageHash} on it.
 Documentation for signature generation:
 - with https://web3js.readthedocs.io/en/v1.3.4/web3-eth-accounts.html#sign[Web3.js]
 - with https://docs.ethers.io/v5/api/signer/#Signer-signMessage[ethers]
 _Available since v4.3._

@dev https://eips.ethereum.org/EIPS/eip-712[EIP 712] is a standard for hashing and signing of typed structured data.
 The encoding specified in the EIP is very generic, and such a generic implementation in Solidity is not feasible,
 thus this contract does not implement the encoding itself. Protocols need to implement the type-specific encoding
 they need in their contracts using a combination of `abi.encode` and `keccak256`.
 This contract implements the EIP 712 domain separator ({_domainSeparatorV4}) that is used as part of the encoding
 scheme, and the final step of the encoding to obtain the message digest that is then signed via ECDSA
 ({_hashTypedDataV4}).
 The implementation of the domain separator was designed to be as efficient as possible while still properly updating
 the chain id to protect against replay attacks on an eventual fork of the chain.
 NOTE: This contract implements the version of the encoding known as "v4", as implemented by the JSON RPC method
 https://docs.metamask.io/guide/signing-data.html[`eth_signTypedDataV4` in MetaMask].
 _Available since v3.4._

@dev Initializes the domain separator and parameter caches.
 The meaning of `name` and `version` is specified in
 https://eips.ethereum.org/EIPS/eip-712#definition-of-domainseparator[EIP 712]:
 - `name`: the user readable name of the signing domain, i.e. the name of the DApp or the protocol.
 - `version`: the current major version of the signing domain.
 NOTE: These parameters cannot be changed except through a xref:learn::upgrading-smart-contracts.adoc[smart
 contract upgrade].
@dev Returns the domain separator for the current chain.

@dev These functions deal with verification of Merkle Tree proofs.
 The tree and the proofs can be generated using our
 https://github.com/OpenZeppelin/merkle-tree[JavaScript library].
 You will find a quickstart guide in the readme.
 WARNING: You should avoid using leaf values that are 64 bytes long prior to
 hashing, or use a hash function other than keccak256 for hashing leaves.
 This is because the concatenation of a sorted pair of internal nodes in
 the merkle tree could be reinterpreted as a leaf value.
 OpenZeppelin's JavaScript library generates merkle trees that are safe
 against this attack out of the box.

@dev Returns true if a `leaf` can be proved to be a part of a Merkle tree
 defined by `root`. For this, a `proof` must be provided, containing
 sibling hashes on the branch from the leaf to the root of the tree. Each
 pair of leaves and each pair of pre-images are assumed to be sorted.

@dev Calldata version of {verify}
 _Available since v4.7._

@dev Returns the rebuilt hash obtained by traversing a Merkle tree up
 from `leaf` using `proof`. A `proof` is valid if and only if the rebuilt
 hash matches the root of the tree. When processing the proof, the pairs
 of leafs & pre-images are assumed to be sorted.
 _Available since v4.4._

@dev Calldata version of {processProof}

@dev Returns the root of a tree reconstructed from `leaves` and sibling nodes in `proof`. The reconstruction
 proceeds by incrementally reconstructing all inner nodes by combining a leaf/inner node with either another
 leaf/inner node or a proof sibling node, depending on whether each `proofFlags` item is true or false
 respectively.
 CAUTION: Not all merkle trees admit multiproofs. To use multiproofs, it is sufficient to ensure that: 1) the tree
 is complete (but not necessarily perfect), 2) the leaves to be proven are in the opposite order they are in the
 tree (i.e., as seen from right to left starting at the deepest layer and continuing at the next layer).
 _Available since v4.7._

Note that because there is a single `nonReentrant` guard, functions marked as `nonReentrant` may not call one another. This can be worked around by making those functions `private`, and then adding `external` `nonReentrant` entry points to them. TIP: If you would like to learn more about reentrancy and alternative ways to protect against it, check out our blog post https://blog.openzeppelin.com/reentrancy-after-istanbul/[Reentrancy After Istanbul].

Approval(address,address,uint256).details: Emitted when the allowance of a `spender` for an `owner` is set by a call to {approve}. `value` is the new allowance.

Transfer(address,address,uint256).details: Emitted when `value` tokens are moved from one account (`from`) to another (`to`). Note that `value` may be zero.

allowance(address,address).details: Returns the remaining number of tokens that `spender` will be allowed to spend on behalf of `owner` through {transferFrom}. This is zero by default. This value changes when {approve} or {transferFrom} are called.

approve(address,uint256).details: Sets `amount` as the allowance of `spender` over the caller's tokens. Returns a boolean value indicating whether the operation succeeded. IMPORTANT: Beware that changing an allowance with this method brings the risk that someone may use both the old and the new allowance by unfortunate transaction ordering. One possible solution to mitigate this race condition is to first reduce the spender's allowance to 0 and set the desired value afterwards: https://github.com/ethereum/EIPs/issues/20#issuecomment-263524729 Emits an {Approval} event.

transfer(address,uint256).details: Moves `amount` tokens from the caller's account to `to`. Returns a boolean value indicating whether the operation succeeded. Emits a {Transfer} event.

transferFrom(address,address,uint256).details: Moves `amount` tokens from `from` to `to` using the allowance mechanism. `amount` is then deducted from the caller's allowance. Returns a boolean value indicating whether the operation succeeded. Emits a {Transfer} event.

devdoc.details: https://eips.ethereum.org/EIPS/eip-712[EIP 712] is a standard for hashing and signing of typed structured data. The encoding specified in the EIP is very generic, and such a generic implementation in Solidity is not feasible, thus this contract does not implement the encoding itself. Protocols need to implement the type-specific encoding they need in their contracts using a combination of `abi.encode` and `keccak256`. This contract implements the EIP 712 domain separator ({_domainSeparatorV4}) that is used as part of the encoding scheme, and the final step of the encoding to obtain the message digest that is then signed via ECDSA ({_hashTypedDataV4}). The implementation of the domain separator was designed to be as efficient as possible while still properly updating the chain id to protect against replay attacks on an eventual fork of the chain. NOTE: This contract implements the version of the encoding known as "v4", as implemented by the JSON RPC method https://docs.metamask.io/guide/signing-data.html[`eth_signTypedDataV4` in MetaMask]. _Available since v3.4._

constructor.details: Initializes the domain separator and parameter caches. The meaning of `name` and `version` is specified in https://eips.ethereum.org/EIPS/eip-712#definition-of-domainseparator[EIP 712]: - `name`: the user readable name of the signing domain, i.e. the name of the DApp or the protocol. - `version`: the current major version of the signing domain. NOTE: These parameters cannot be changed except through a xref:learn::upgrading-smart-contracts.adoc[smart contract upgrade].

devdoc.details: These functions deal with verification of Merkle Tree proofs. The tree and the proofs can be generated using our https://github.com/OpenZeppelin/merkle-tree[JavaScript library]. You will find a quickstart guide in the readme. WARNING: You should avoid using leaf values that are 64 bytes long prior to hashing, or use a hash function other than keccak256 for hashing leaves. This is because the concatenation of a sorted pair of internal nodes in the merkle tree could be reinterpreted as a leaf value. OpenZeppelin's JavaScript library generates merkle trees that are safe against this attack out of the box.

type(uint256).max,\n        type(uint256).max,\n        type(uint256).max,\n        type(uint256).max,\n        type(uint256).max\n    ];\n\n    uint256 public publicMintStartTime = type(uint256).max;\n    uint256 public mintlistStartTime = type(uint256).max;\n    uint256 public claimsStartTime = type(uint256).max;\n\n    /// @notice The primary merkle root\n    bytes32 public claimlistMintedPerSize;\n\n    /**\n     * @dev Create the contract and set the initial baseURI\n     * @param _runiverseLand address the initial base URI for the token metadata URL\n     */\n    constructor(IRuniverseLand _runiverseLand) {\n        setRuniverseLand(_runiverseLand);\n        setVaultAddress(payable(msg.sender));\n        signer = address(0);\n    }\n\n    /**\n     * @dev since the begining.\n     * @return getPlotsAvailablePerSize array uint256 of 5 elements.\n     */\n    function getPlotsAvailablePerSize()\n        external\n        view\n        returns (uint256[] memory)\n    {\n        return plotsAvailablePerSize;\n    }\n\n    /**\n     * @dev returns the eth cost of each plot.\n     * @return getPlotPrices array uint256 of 5 elements.\n     */\n    function getPlotPrices() external view returns (uint256[] memory) {\n        return plotPrices;\n    }\n\n    /**\n     * @dev returns the plot type of a token id.\n     * @param tokenId uint256 token id.\n     * @return getPlotPrices uint256 plot type.\n     */\n    function getTokenIdPlotType(\n        uint256 tokenId\n    ) external pure returns (uint256) {\n        return tokenId & 255;\n    }\n\n    /**\n     * @dev return the total number of minted plots\n     * @return getTotalMintedLands uint256 number of minted plots.\n     */\n    function getTotalMintedLands() external view returns (uint256) {\n        uint256 totalMintedLands;\n        totalMintedLands =\n            plotsMinted[0] +\n            plotsMinted[1] +\n            plotsMinted[2] +\n            plotsMinted[3] +\n            plotsMinted[4];\n        return totalMintedLands;\n    }\n\n    /**\n     * @dev return the total number of minted plots of each size.\n     * @return getTotalMintedLandsBySize array uint256 number of minted plots of each size.\n     */\n\n    function getTotalMintedLandsBySize()\n        external\n        view\n        returns (uint256[] memory)\n    {\n        uint256[] memory plotsMintedBySize = new uint256[](5);\n\n        plotsMintedBySize[0] = plotsMinted[0];\n        plotsMintedBySize[1] = plotsMinted[1];\n        plotsMintedBySize[2] = plotsMinted[2];\n        plotsMintedBySize[3] = plotsMinted[3];\n        plotsMintedBySize[4] = plotsMinted[4];\n\n        return plotsMintedBySize;\n    }\n\n    /**\n     * @dev returns the number of plots left of each size.\n     * @return getAvailableLands array uint256 of 5 elements.\n     */\n    function getAvailableLands() external view returns (uint256[] memory) {\n        uint256[] memory plotsAvailableBySize = new uint256[](5);\n\n        plotsAvailableBySize[0] = plotsAvailablePerSize[0] - plotsMinted[0];\n        plotsAvailableBySize[1] = plotsAvailablePerSize[1] - plotsMinted[1];\n        plotsAvailableBySize[2] = plotsAvailablePerSize[2] - plotsMinted[2];\n        plotsAvailableBySize[3] = plotsAvailablePerSize[3] - plotsMinted[3];\n        plotsAvailableBySize[4] = plotsAvailablePerSize[4] - plotsMinted[4];\n\n        return plotsAvailableBySize;\n    }\n\n    /**\n     * @dev Verifies if the signature corresponds to the signer.\n     * @param _message Message to verify with signature.\n     * @param _signature Signature used to verify the message.\n     * @return bool Returns if the signature is valid or not.\n     */\n    function verify(\n        string memory _message,\n        bytes memory _signature\n    ) public view returns (bool) {\n        bytes32 messageHash = getMessageHash(_message);\n        bytes32 ethSignedMessageHash = getEthSignedMessageHash(messageHash);\n\n        return recover(ethSignedMessageHash, _signature) == signer;\n    }\n\n    /**\n     * @dev Returns the message hash that is signed to create the signature.\n     * @param _message Message to be hashed.\n     * @return bytes32 Hash of the message.\n     */\n    function getMessageHash(\n        string memory _message\n    ) public pure returns (bytes32) {\n        return keccak256(abi.encodePacked(_message));\n    }\n\n    /**\n     * @dev Returns the message hash that is signed to create the signature.\n     * @param _messageHash Hash of the message to be signed.\n     * @return bytes32 Hash of the message.\n     */\n    function getEthSignedMessageHash(\n        bytes32 _messageHash\n    ) public pure returns (bytes32) {\n        return\n            keccak256(\n                abi.encodePacked(\n                    \"\\x19Ethereum Signed Message:\\n32\",\n                    _messageHash\n                )\n            );\n    }\n\n    /**\n     * @dev Split signature and recover signer address.\n     * @param _ethSignedMessageHash Hash of the signed message.\n     * @param _signature Signature to split.\n     * @return address Address of the signer.\n     */\n    function recover(\n        bytes32 _ethSignedMessageHash,\n        bytes memory _signature\n    ) private pure returns (address) {\n        (bytes32 r, bytes32 s, uint8 v) = splitSignature(_signature);\n\n        (address recovered, ECDSA.RecoverError err) = ECDSA.tryRecover(\n            _ethSignedMessageHash,\n            v,\n            r,\n            s\n        );\n        return recovered;\n    }\n\n    /**\n     * @dev Split signature into `r`, `s` and `v` variables, used by recover method.\n     * @param _signature Signature to split.\n     * @return r\n     * @return s\n     * @return v\n     */\n    function splitSignature(\n        bytes memory _signature\n    ) internal pure returns (bytes32 r, bytes32 s, uint8 v) {\n        require(_signature.length == 65, \"Invalid signature length!\");\n\n        assembly {\n            // First 32 bytes stores the length of the signature\n            r := mload(add(_signature, 32))\n            // Next 32 bytes stores the length of the signature\n            s := mload(add(_signature, 64))\n            // Final byte stores the signature type\n            v := byte(0, mload(add(_signature, 96)))\n        }\n    }\n\n    /**\n     * @dev Method to verify a message and mint an RuniverseItem to an address. Used for public minting.\n     * @param signature Signature used to verify the message.\n     * @param plotSize type of the land token to be minted.\n     */\n    function verifyAndMint(\n        bytes memory signature,\n        IRuniverseLand.PlotSize plotSize\n    ) public {\n        string memory message = string.concat(\n            Strings.toHexString(msg.sender),\n            \"_\",\n            Strings.toString(uint256(plotSize)),\n            \"_\",\n            Strings.toString(nonce[msg.sender])\n        );\n\n        require(this.verify(message, signature), \"Bad signature\");\n\n        // Get next id per type\n        uint256 tokenId = ownerGetNextTokenId(plotSize);\n        ++plotsMinted[uint256(plotSize)];\n\n        // Mint token\n        runiverseLand.mintTokenId(msg.sender, tokenId, plotSize);\n\n        // Update nonce\n        nonce[msg.sender] += 1;\n    }\n\n    /**\n     * @dev mint public method to mint when the whitelist (mintlist) is active.\n     * @param _who address address that is minting.\n     * @param _leaf bytes32 merkle leaf.\n     * @param _merkleProof bytes32[] merkle proof.\n     * @return mintlisted bool success mint.\n     */\n    function mintlisted(\n        address _who,\n        bytes32 _leaf,\n        bytes32[] calldata _merkleProof\n    ) external view returns (bool) {\n        bytes32 node = keccak256(abi.encodePacked(_who));\n\n        if (node != _leaf) return false;\n        if (\n            MerkleProof.verify(_merkleProof, mintlistMerkleRoot1, _leaf) ||\n            MerkleProof.verify(_merkleProof, mintlistMerkleRoot2, _leaf)\n        ) {\n            return true;\n        }\n        return false;\n    }\n\n    /**\n     * @dev public method  for public minting.\n     * @param plotSize PlotSize enum with plot size.\n     * @param numPlots uint256 number of plots to be minted.\n     */\n    function mint(\n        IRuniverseLand.PlotSize plotSize,\n        uint256 numPlots\n    ) external payable nonReentrant {\n        if (!publicStarted()) {\n            revert WrongDateForProcess({\n                correct_date: publicMintStartTime,\n                current_date: block.timestamp\n            });\n        }\n        if (numPlots <= 0 || numPlots > 20) {\n            revert IncorrectPurchaseLimit();\n        }\n        _mintTokensCheckingValue(plotSize, numPlots, msg.sender);\n    }\n\n    /**\n     * @dev public method to mint when the whitelist (mintlist) is active.\n     * @param plotSize PlotSize enum with plot size.\n     * @param numPlots uint256 number of plots to be minted.\n     * @param claimedMaxPlots uint256 maximum number of plots of plotSize size  that the address mint.\n     * @param _merkleProof bytes32[] merkle proof.\n     */\n    function mintlistMint(\n        IRuniverseLand.PlotSize plotSize,\n        uint256 numPlots,\n        uint256 claimedMaxPlots,\n        bytes32[] calldata _merkleProof\n    ) external payable nonReentrant {\n        if (!mintlistStarted()) {\n            revert WrongDateForProcess({\n                correct_date: mintlistStartTime,\n                current_date: block.timestamp\n            });\n        }\n        if (numPlots <= 0 && numPlots > 20) {\n            revert IncorrectPurchaseLimit();\n        }\n        // verify allowlist\n        bytes32 _leaf = keccak256(\n            abi.encodePacked(\n                msg.sender,\n                \":\",\n                uint256(plotSize),\n                \":\",\n                claimedMaxPlots\n            )\n        );\n\n        require(\n            MerkleProof.verify(_merkleProof, mintlistMerkleRoot1, _leaf) ||\n                MerkleProof.verify(_merkleProof, mintlistMerkleRoot2, _leaf),\n            \"Invalid proof.\"\n        );\n\n        mapping(uint256 => uint256)\n            storage mintedPerSize = mintlistMintedPerSize[msg.sender];\n\n        require(\n            mintedPerSize[uint256(plotSize)] + numPlots <= claimedMaxPlots, // this is verified by the merkle proof\n            \"Minting more than allowed\"\n        );\n        mintedPerSize[uint256(plotSize)] += numPlots;\n        _mintTokensCheckingValue(plotSize, numPlots, msg.sender);\n    }\n\n    /**\n     * @dev public method to claim a plot, only when (claimlist) is active.\n     * @param plotSize PlotSize enum with plot size.\n     * @param numPlots uint256 number of plots to be minted.\n     * @param claimedMaxPlots uint256 maximum number of plots of plotSize size  that the address mint.\n     * @param _merkleProof bytes32[] merkle proof.\n     */\n    function claimlistMint(\n        IRuniverseLand.PlotSize plotSize,\n        uint256 numPlots,\n        uint256 claimedMaxPlots,\n        bytes32[] calldata _merkleProof\n    ) external payable nonReentrant {\n        if (!claimsStarted()) {\n            revert WrongDateForProcess({\n                correct_date: claimsStartTime,\n                current_date: block.timestamp\n            });\n        }\n\n        // verify allowlist\n        bytes32 _leaf = keccak256(\n            abi.encodePacked(\n                msg.sender,\n                \":\",\n                uint256(plotSize),\n                \":\",\n                claimedMaxPlots\n            )\n        );\n\n        require(\n            MerkleProof.verify(_merkleProof, claimlistMerkleRoot, _leaf),\n            \"Invalid proof.\"\n        );\n\n        mapping(uint256 => uint256)\n            storage mintedPerSize = claimlistMintedPerSize[msg.sender];\n\n        require(\n            mintedPerSize[uint256(plotSize)] + numPlots <= claimedMaxPlots, // this is verified by the merkle proof\n            \"Claiming more than allowed\"\n        );\n        mintedPerSize[uint256(plotSize)] += numPlots;\n        _mintTokens(plotSize, numPlots, msg.sender);\n    }\n\n    /**\n     * @dev checks if the amount sent is correct. Continue minting if it is correct.\n     * @param plotSize PlotSize enum with plot size.\n     * @param numPlots uint256 number of plots to be minted.\n     * @param recipient address  address that sent the mint.\n     */\n    function _mintTokensCheckingValue(\n        IRuniverseLand.PlotSize plotSize,\n        uint256 numPlots,\n        address recipient\n    ) private {\n        if (plotPrices[uint256(plotSize)] <= 0) {\n            revert MisconfiguredPrices();\n        }\n        require(\n            msg.value == plotPrices[uint256(plotSize)] * numPlots,\n            \"Ether value sent is not accurate\"\n        );\n        _mintTokens(plotSize, numPlots, recipient);\n    }\n\n    /**\n     * @dev checks if there are plots available. Used for private minting.\n     * @param plotSizes PlotSize[] enums with plot sizes.\n     * @param recipients address[]  addresses where the token will be transferred.\n     */\n    function ownerMint(\n        IRuniverseLand.PlotSize[] calldata plotSizes,\n        address[] calldata recipients\n    ) external onlyOwner {\n        require(\n            plotSizes.length == recipients.length,\n            \"Arrays should have the same size\"\n        );\n        for (uint256 i; i < recipients.length; ++i) {\n            _mintTokens(plotSizes[i], 1, recipients[i]);\n        }\n    }\n\n    /**\n     * @dev Encodes the next token id.\n     * @param plotSize PlotSize enum with plot size.\n     * @return ownerGetNextTokenId uint256 encoded next toknId.\n     */\n    function ownerGetNextTokenId(\n        IRuniverseLand.PlotSize plotSize\n    ) private view returns (uint256) {\n        uint256 globalCounter = plotsMinted[0] +\n            plotsMinted[1] +\n plotSizeLocalOffset[uint256(plotSize)];\n        require(localCounter <= 4294967295, \"Local index overflow\");\n        require(uint256(plotSize) <= 255, \"Plot index overflow\");\n\n        return function setMintlistMerkleRoot1(bytes32 newMerkleRoot) external onlyOwner {\n        mintlistMerkleRoot1 = newMerkleRoot;\n    }\n\n    /**\n     * @dev Assigns a merkle root to the second tree for This value will be added to the local id of each plot size  when a token of some size is generated.\n     * @param _newPlotSizeLocalOffset uint256[] offsets\n     */\n    function setLocalIdOffsets(\n sended_values: _newPlotSizeLocalOffset.length,\n                expected: 5\n            });\n        }\n        if (mintlistStarted()) {\n            revert DeniedProcessDuringMinting();\n        }\n        plotSizeLocalOffset = _newPlotSizeLocalOffset;\n    }\n\n    /**\n     * @dev Assigns the new plot prices for each plot size.\n     * @param _newPrices uint256[] plots prices.\n     */\n    function setPrices(uint256[] calldata _newPrices) external onlyOwner {\n        if (mintlistStarted()) {\n            revert DeniedProcessDuringMinting();\n        }\n        if (_newPrices.length <   /**\n     * @notice Withdraw funds to the vault using sendValue\n     * @param _amount uint256 the amount to withdraw\n     */\n    function withdraw(uint256 _amount) external onlyOwner {\n        (bool success, ) = vault.call{value: _amount}(\"\");\n        require(success, \"withdraw was not succesfull\");\n    }\n\n    /**\n     * @notice Withdraw all the funds to the vault using sendValue\n }\n\n    /**\n     * @notice Transfer amount to a token.\n     * @param _token IERC20 token to transfer\n     * @param _amount uint256 amount to transfer\n     */\n    function forwardERC20s(IERC20 }\n\n    /// Wrong date for process, Come back on `correct_data` for complete this successfully\n    /// @param correct_date date when the public/ mint is on.\n    /// @param current_date date when
